The decision instants themselves (decision_utc) were honestly pre-game -- decision_time_for_game's own guard had nothing to object to -- but the RUN that wrote these rows did not happen until the observed write instant below, well after this game's first pitch. Prior to this fix, recorded_utc equalled decision_utc on every row (B1), so the ledger carried no evidence of when these rows were actually written; the write instant below is reconstructed from the commit that added these rows (git show -s --format=%cI 41c74c7399e68a8657183876bbf5cc3c31e6c2de) and the file's own mtime at that commit, both consistent. src.engine.slate.run_slate now refuses (skips, does not write) any game already commenced at the actual write instant in LIVE mode -- these rows were written before that guard existed and would be refused if the same run happened today. This row does not alter, replace, or remove the original decision rows -- the ledger is append-only and its history is preserved exactly as written; this is additional evidence appended after the fact, not a correction of the original bytes.
note: Appended by the B1/B2 fix (session https://claude.ai/code/session_01BB6CEj23fhPMVV2gLhkqz4). thesis: This pick carries the market's own probability and no edge, by construction. Its p_model is the board's own de-vigged consensus for this exact selection, republished unchanged by analyze()'s PROJECT phase under the identity map -- zero fitted parameters, no recalibration intercept, no Platt, no isotonic refit (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md §2). Because the probability IS the price, diffing the two would measure nothing: edge_bps is structurally None and no edge is claimed. It is published as a calibration reference -- how good the market's own number is -- never as a reason to bet.

thesis: This is a DELIBERATE CONTROL, not a pick anyone should follow: it takes the under in every game, always, on no information at all. The direction was fixed in code before any board was read and is never derived from price, a clock or a search. Its p_model is a declared coin flip (provenance=placeholder), so no edge_bps can ever be computed for it -- that is the point: it is the baseline every real system has to beat (src.engine.adapters.evolab_system).

Its p_model is the board's own de-vigged consensus for this exact selection, republished unchanged by analyze()'s PROJECT phase under the identity map -- zero fitted parameters, no recalibration intercept, no Platt, no isotonic refit (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md §2). Because the probability IS the price, diffing the two would measure nothing: edge_bps is structurally None and no edge is claimed. It is published as a calibration reference -- how good the market's own number is -- never as a reason to bet.

thesis: This is a DELIBERATE CONTROL, not a pick anyone should follow: it takes the under in every game, always, on no information at all. Its p_model is a declared coin flip (provenance=placeholder), so no edge_bps can ever be computed for it -- that is the point: it is the baseline every real system has to beat (src.engine.adapters.evolab_system).

mechanism_predicates.claim: the harder-throwing starter -- the one this side is backed BECAUSE its opponent has to face him -- holds that opposing lineup below the league rate starters allow
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_starter_vs_opposing_lineup

thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) starter_velocity_gap -- how far the opposing starter's fastball sits above league pace (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 3.64 mph, home 0.91 mph (this game's own values rest on: away over 268 measured fastballs; home over 167 measured fastballs); a gap of 2.74 mph, clearing the threshold of 1.96 mph (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,149 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter whose fastball sits above league pace is holding stuff the season line has not caught up to, so the lineup facing the harder thrower is the disadvantaged side; velocity leads results and the market prices results. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 56ba4bb647b80640.)

Its p_model is the board's own de-vigged consensus for this exact selection, republished unchanged by analyze()'s PROJECT phase under the identity map -- zero fitted parameters, no recalibration intercept, no Platt, no isotonic refit (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md §2). It is published as a calibration reference -- how good the market's own number is -- never as a reason to bet.

mechanism_predicates.claim: the harder-throwing starter -- the one this side is backed BECAUSE its opponent has to face him -- holds that opposing lineup below the league rate starters allow
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_starter_vs_opposing_lineup

thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) starter_velocity_gap -- how far the opposing starter's fastball sits above league pace (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 0.79 mph, home -1.59 mph (this game's own values rest on: away over 162 measured fastballs; home over 190 measured fastballs); a gap of 2.38 mph, clearing the threshold of 1.96 mph (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,149 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter whose fastball sits above league pace is holding stuff the season line has not caught up to, so the lineup facing the harder thrower is the disadvantaged side; velocity leads results and the market prices results. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 56ba4bb647b80640.)

mechanism_predicates.claim: the harder-throwing starter -- the one this side is backed BECAUSE its opponent has to face him -- holds that opposing lineup below the league rate starters allow
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_starter_vs_opposing_lineup

thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) starter_velocity_gap -- how far the opposing starter's fastball sits above league pace (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 0.79 mph, home -1.59 mph (this game's own values rest on: away over 162 measured fastballs; home over 190 measured fastballs); a gap of 2.38 mph, clearing the threshold of 1.96 mph (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,149 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter whose fastball sits above league pace is holding stuff the season line has not caught up to, so the lineup facing the harder thrower is the disadvantaged side; velocity leads results and the market prices results. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 56ba4bb647b80640.)

thesis: Backing the away side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) lineup_platoon_share -- the share of the posted lineup holding the platoon advantage over the starter it faces (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 83.3%, home 60.0% (this game's own values rest on: away over 9 lineup slots; home over 9 lineup slots); a gap of 23.3 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 22.2 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,856 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: the classic exploitation: a lineup posted one-handed against a starter it holds the platoon advantage over gets more of its plate appearances in the favourable split than the club-level season line the market prices ever reflects. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). mechanism_predicates.claim: the harder-throwing starter -- the one this side is backed BECAUSE its opponent has to face him -- holds that opposing lineup below the league rate starters allow
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_starter_vs_opposing_lineup

thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) starter_velocity_gap -- how far the opposing starter's fastball sits above league pace (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 2.17 mph, home -0.92 mph (this game's own values rest on: away over 182 measured fastballs; home over 179 measured fastballs); a gap of 3.08 mph, clearing the threshold of 1.96 mph (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,149 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter whose fastball sits above league pace is holding stuff the season line has not caught up to, so the lineup facing the harder thrower is the disadvantaged side; velocity leads results and the market prices results. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 56ba4bb647b80640.)

mechanism_predicates.claim: the harder-throwing starter -- the one this side is backed BECAUSE its opponent has to face him -- holds that opposing lineup below the league rate starters allow
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_starter_vs_opposing_lineup

thesis: Backing the away side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) starter_velocity_gap -- how far the opposing starter's fastball sits above league pace (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 0.41 mph, home 3.67 mph (this game's own values rest on: away over 219 measured fastballs; home over 265 measured fastballs); a gap of 3.26 mph, clearing the threshold of 1.96 mph (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,149 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter whose fastball sits above league pace is holding stuff the season line has not caught up to, so the lineup facing the harder thrower is the disadvantaged side; velocity leads results and the market prices results. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 56ba4bb647b80640.)

mechanism_predicates.claim: the platoon-advantaged lineup reaches base against the starter it was posted against at or above the league rate starters allow
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_lineup_vs_opposing_starter

thesis: Backing the away side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) lineup_platoon_share -- the share of the posted lineup holding the platoon advantage over the starter it faces (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 83.3%, home 57.1% (this game's own values rest on: away over 9 lineup slots; home over 9 lineup slots); a gap of 26.2 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 22.2 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,856 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: the classic exploitation: a lineup posted one-handed against a starter it holds the platoon advantage over gets more of its plate appearances in the favourable split than the club-level season line the market prices ever reflects. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 4a7700d36b3855ab.)

mechanism_predicates.claim: the harder-throwing starter -- the one this side is backed BECAUSE its opponent has to face him -- holds that opposing lineup below the league rate starters allow
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_starter_vs_opposing_lineup

thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) starter_velocity_gap -- how far the opposing starter's fastball sits above league pace (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 6.35 mph, home -1.47 mph (this game's own values rest on: away over 282 measured fastballs; home over 207 measured fastballs); a gap of 7.81 mph, clearing the threshold of 1.96 mph (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,149 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter whose fastball sits above league pace is holding stuff the season line has not caught up to, so the lineup facing the harder thrower is the disadvantaged side; velocity leads results and the market prices results. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 56ba4bb647b80640.)

thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) starter_velocity_gap -- how far the opposing starter's fastball sits above league pace (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 2.17 mph, home -0.92 mph (this game's own values rest on: away over 182 measured fastballs; home over 179 measured fastballs); a gap of 3.08 mph, clearing the threshold of 1.96 mph (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,149 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter whose fastball sits above league pace is holding stuff the season line has not caught up to, so the lineup facing the harder thrower is the disadvantaged side; velocity leads results and the market prices results. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 999a7baa84ce385c.)

mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_lineup_vs_opposing_starter

thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) lineup_vs_primary_pitch -- this lineup's measured production against the primary pitch of the starter it faces (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 0.307 wOBA, home 0.358 wOBA (this game's own values rest on: away over 1,584 plate appearances; home over 977 plate appearances); a gap of 0.051 wOBA, clearing the threshold of 0.029 wOBA (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,048 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter who leans on one pitch, against a lineup that has measurably hit that pitch, has nowhere to hide for eighteen outs; the market prices his season line, not tonight's specific collision. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 8974e1cb85d58bcb.)

thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 2 pre-registered signals fired: (1) primary_pitch_share -- the share of pitches the opposing starter throws with his single most-used offering (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 29.1%, home 51.0% (this game's own values rest on: away over 10,138 pitches; home over 7,103 pitches); a gap of 21.9 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 9.7 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,061 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: concentration in one pitch is predictability: the more of a starter's arsenal is a single offering, the more of the lineup's preparation transfers, and pitch-level lean is not a term in any club-level price. (2) top_minus_bottom -- this lineup's top-of-order minus bottom-of-order strength (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 0.014 wOBA, home 0.039 wOBA (this game's own values rest on: away over 5,635 plate-appearance denominators; home over 4,662 plate-appearance denominators); a gap of 0.025 wOBA, clearing the threshold of 0.023 wOBA (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,838 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a top-heavy order concentrates its best bats where the extra plate appearances go, and club-level pricing averages that concentration away; the weakest mechanism of the six, kept because V4 stated it before seeing its result. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). mechanism_predicates.claim: the harder-throwing starter -- the one this side is backed BECAUSE its opponent has to face him -- holds that opposing lineup below the league rate starters allow
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_starter_vs_opposing_lineup

thesis: Backing the away side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) starter_velocity_gap -- how far the opposing starter's fastball sits above league pace (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 0.41 mph, home 3.67 mph (this game's own values rest on: away over 219 measured fastballs; home over 265 measured fastballs); a gap of 3.26 mph, clearing the threshold of 1.96 mph (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,149 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter whose fastball sits above league pace is holding stuff the season line has not caught up to, so the lineup facing the harder thrower is the disadvantaged side; velocity leads results and the market prices results. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 56ba4bb647b80640.)

mechanism_predicates.claim: the harder-throwing starter -- the one this side is backed BECAUSE its opponent has to face him -- holds that opposing lineup below the league rate starters allow
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_starter_vs_opposing_lineup

thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) starter_velocity_gap -- how far the opposing starter's fastball sits above league pace (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 3.24 mph, home -2.07 mph (this game's own values rest on: away over 206 measured fastballs; home over 259 measured fastballs); a gap of 5.31 mph, clearing the threshold of 1.96 mph (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,149 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter whose fastball sits above league pace is holding stuff the season line has not caught up to, so the lineup facing the harder thrower is the disadvantaged side; velocity leads results and the market prices results. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 56ba4bb647b80640.)

thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) top_minus_bottom -- this lineup's top-of-order minus bottom-of-order strength (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 0.028 wOBA, home 0.056 wOBA (this game's own values rest on: away over 3,737 plate-appearance denominators; home over 5,756 plate-appearance denominators); a gap of 0.028 wOBA, clearing the threshold of 0.023 wOBA (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,838 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a top-heavy order concentrates its best bats where the extra plate appearances go, and club-level pricing averages that concentration away; the weakest mechanism of the six, kept because V4 stated it before seeing its result. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome ed2b9ec19d3b9b9a.)

This pick carries the market's own probability and no edge, by construction. Its p_model is the board's own de-vigged consensus for this exact selection, republished unchanged by analyze()'s PROJECT phase under the identity map -- zero fitted parameters, no recalibration intercept, no Platt, no isotonic refit (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md §2). Because the probability IS the price, diffing the two would measure nothing: edge_bps is structurally None and no edge is claimed. It is published as a calibration reference -- how good the market's own number is -- never as a reason to bet.

This is a DELIBERATE CONTROL, not a pick anyone should follow: it takes the home side of the moneyline in every game, always, on no information at all. The direction and the p_model are fixed conventions written down in code before any board was read -- never fit, never derived from price or a clock -- and provenance=placeholder means no edge_bps can ever be computed for it. That is the point: it is the baseline every real system has to beat (src.engine.glue).

This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter who leans on one pitch, against a lineup that has measurably hit that pitch, has nowhere to hide for eighteen outs; the market prices his season line, not tonight's specific collision. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome e8c58d079df7ecdd.)

This pick carries the market's own probability and no edge, by construction. Its p_model is the board's own de-vigged consensus for this exact selection, republished unchanged by analyze()'s PROJECT phase under the identity map -- zero fitted parameters, no recalibration intercept, no Platt, no isotonic refit (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md §2). Because the probability IS the price, diffing the two would measure nothing: edge_bps is structurally None and no edge is claimed. It is published as a calibration reference -- how good the market's own number is -- never as a reason to bet.

mechanism_predicates.claim: the harder-throwing starter -- the one this side is backed BECAUSE its opponent has to face him -- holds that opposing lineup below the league rate starters allow
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_starter_vs_opposing_lineup

thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) starter_velocity_gap -- how far the opposing starter's fastball sits above league pace (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 3.24 mph, home -2.07 mph (this game's own values rest on: away over 206 measured fastballs; home over 259 measured fastballs); a gap of 5.31 mph, clearing the threshold of 1.96 mph (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,149 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter whose fastball sits above league pace is holding stuff the season line has not caught up to, so the lineup facing the harder thrower is the disadvantaged side; velocity leads results and the market prices results. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 56ba4bb647b80640.)

thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 2 pre-registered signals fired: (1) lineup_vs_primary_pitch -- this lineup's measured production against the primary pitch of the starter it faces (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 0.295 wOBA, home 0.358 wOBA (this game's own values rest on: away over 1,493 plate appearances; home over 977 plate appearances); a gap of 0.063 wOBA, clearing the threshold of 0.053 wOBA (rung 2 of 3, the 75th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,048 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter who leans on one pitch, against a lineup that has measurably hit that pitch, has nowhere to hide for eighteen outs; the market prices his season line, not tonight's specific collision. (2) primary_pitch_share -- the share of pitches the opposing starter throws with his single most-used offering (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 29.1%, home 51.0% (this game's own values rest on: away over 10,138 pitches; home over 7,103 pitches); a gap of 21.9 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 9.7 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,061 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: concentration in one pitch is predictability: the more of a starter's arsenal is a single offering, the more of the lineup's preparation transfers, and pitch-level lean is not a term in any club-level price. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 7be45f28a9c9312a.)

thesis: Backing the away side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) starter_velocity_gap -- how far the opposing starter's fastball sits above league pace (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 0.41 mph, home 3.67 mph (this game's own values rest on: away over 219 measured fastballs; home over 265 measured fastballs); a gap of 3.26 mph, clearing the threshold of 1.96 mph (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,149 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter whose fastball sits above league pace is holding stuff the season line has not caught up to, so the lineup facing the harder thrower is the disadvantaged side; velocity leads results and the market prices results. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 2 pre-registered signals fired: (1) lineup_vs_primary_pitch -- this lineup's measured production against the primary pitch of the starter it faces (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 0.295 wOBA, home 0.358 wOBA (this game's own values rest on: away over 1,493 plate appearances; home over 977 plate appearances); a gap of 0.063 wOBA, clearing the threshold of 0.053 wOBA (rung 2 of 3, the 75th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,048 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter who leans on one pitch, against a lineup that has measurably hit that pitch, has nowhere to hide for eighteen outs; the market prices his season line, not tonight's specific collision. (2) primary_pitch_share -- the share of pitches the opposing starter throws with his single most-used offering (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 29.1%, home 51.0% (this game's own values rest on: away over 10,138 pitches; home over 7,103 pitches); a gap of 21.9 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 9.7 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,061 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: concentration in one pitch is predictability: the more of a starter's arsenal is a single offering, the more of the lineup's preparation transfers, and pitch-level lean is not a term in any club-level price. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). mechanism_predicates.claim: the harder-throwing starter -- the one this side is backed BECAUSE its opponent has to face him -- holds that opposing lineup below the league rate starters allow
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_starter_vs_opposing_lineup

thesis: Backing the away side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) starter_velocity_gap -- how far the opposing starter's fastball sits above league pace (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 0.41 mph, home 3.67 mph (this game's own values rest on: away over 219 measured fastballs; home over 265 measured fastballs); a gap of 3.26 mph, clearing the threshold of 1.96 mph (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,149 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter whose fastball sits above league pace is holding stuff the season line has not caught up to, so the lineup facing the harder thrower is the disadvantaged side; velocity leads results and the market prices results. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 56ba4bb647b80640.)

thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) top_minus_bottom -- this lineup's top-of-order minus bottom-of-order strength (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 0.040 wOBA, home 0.083 wOBA (this game's own values rest on: away over 4,262 plate-appearance denominators; home over 1,236 plate-appearance denominators); a gap of 0.043 wOBA, clearing the threshold of 0.042 wOBA (rung 2 of 3, the 75th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,838 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a top-heavy order concentrates its best bats where the extra plate appearances go, and club-level pricing averages that concentration away; the weakest mechanism of the six, kept because V4 stated it before seeing its result. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) starter_velocity_gap -- how far the opposing starter's fastball sits above league pace (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 2.74 mph, home -0.53 mph (this game's own values rest on: away over 251 measured fastballs; home over 228 measured fastballs); a gap of 3.27 mph, clearing the threshold of 1.96 mph (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,149 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter whose fastball sits above league pace is holding stuff the season line has not caught up to, so the lineup facing the harder thrower is the disadvantaged side; velocity leads results and the market prices results. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 999a7baa84ce385c.)

This pick carries the market's own probability and no edge, by construction. Its p_model is the board's own de-vigged consensus for this exact selection, republished unchanged by analyze()'s PROJECT phase under the identity map -- zero fitted parameters, no recalibration intercept, no Platt, no isotonic refit (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md §2). Because the probability IS the price, diffing the two would measure nothing: edge_bps is structurally None and no edge is claimed. It is published as a calibration reference -- how good the market's own number is -- never as a reason to bet.

This is a DELIBERATE CONTROL, not a pick anyone should follow: it takes the home side of the moneyline in every game, always, on no information at all. The direction and the p_model are fixed conventions written down in code before any board was read -- never fit, never derived from price or a clock -- and provenance=placeholder means no edge_bps can ever be computed for it. That is the point: it is the baseline every real system has to beat (src.engine.glue).

It is published as a calibration reference -- how good the market's own number is -- never as a reason to bet.

Its p_model is the board's own de-vigged consensus for this exact selection, republished unchanged by analyze()'s PROJECT phase under the identity map -- zero fitted parameters, no recalibration intercept, no Platt, no isotonic refit (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md §2). Because the probability IS the price, diffing the two would measure nothing: edge_bps is structurally None and no edge is claimed. It is published as a calibration reference -- how good the market's own number is -- never as a reason to bet.

Its p_model is the board's own de-vigged consensus for this exact selection, republished unchanged by analyze()'s PROJECT phase under the identity map -- zero fitted parameters, no recalibration intercept, no Platt, no isotonic refit (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md §2). Because the probability IS the price, diffing the two would measure nothing: edge_bps is structurally None and no edge is claimed. It is published as a calibration reference -- how good the market's own number is -- never as a reason to bet.

mechanism_predicates.claim: the lineup that has measurably hit this starter's primary pitch reaches base against him at or above the league rate starters allow -- 'nowhere to hide for eighteen outs', measured over the outs he actually got
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_lineup_vs_opposing_starter

thesis: Backing the away side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) lineup_vs_primary_pitch -- this lineup's measured production against the primary pitch of the starter it faces (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 0.351 wOBA, home 0.304 wOBA (this game's own values rest on: away over 2,782 plate appearances; home over 696 plate appearances); a gap of 0.047 wOBA, clearing the threshold of 0.029 wOBA (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,048 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter who leans on one pitch, against a lineup that has measurably hit that pitch, has nowhere to hide for eighteen outs; the market prices his season line, not tonight's specific collision. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). mechanism_predicates.claim: the ground-ball starter this side is backed behind actually pitched to the ground, at or above the league share of unambiguous batted-ball outs
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_starter_batted_balls

thesis: Backing the away side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) starter_groundball_share -- the opposing starter's career ground-ball share (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 36.9%, home 61.4% (this game's own values rest on: away over 176 batted balls; home over 1,563 batted balls); a gap of 24.5 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 17.5 percentage points (rung 3 of 3, the 90th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,516 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a career ground-ball starter takes the air out of an offence that lives on balls in the air, so the lineup facing the higher ground-ball share is the disadvantaged side and club-level pricing averages the collision out. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 606be696ff199952.)

mechanism_predicates.claim: the lineup that has measurably hit this starter's primary pitch reaches base against him at or above the league rate starters allow -- 'nowhere to hide for eighteen outs', measured over the outs he actually got
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_lineup_vs_opposing_starter

thesis: Backing the away side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) lineup_vs_primary_pitch -- this lineup's measured production against the primary pitch of the starter it faces (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 0.351 wOBA, home 0.304 wOBA (this game's own values rest on: away over 2,782 plate appearances; home over 696 plate appearances); a gap of 0.047 wOBA, clearing the threshold of 0.029 wOBA (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,048 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter who leans on one pitch, against a lineup that has measurably hit that pitch, has nowhere to hide for eighteen outs; the market prices his season line, not tonight's specific collision. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 8974e1cb85d58bcb.)

thesis: This is a DELIBERATE CONTROL, not a pick anyone should follow: it takes the home side of the run line in every game, always, on no information at all. The direction was fixed in code before any board was read and is never derived from price, a clock or a search. thesis: This pick carries the market's own probability and no edge, by construction. mechanism_predicates.claim: the ground-ball starter this side is backed behind actually pitched to the ground, at or above the league share of unambiguous batted-ball outs
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_starter_batted_balls

thesis: Backing the away side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) starter_groundball_share -- the opposing starter's career ground-ball share (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 36.9%, home 61.4% (this game's own values rest on: away over 176 batted balls; home over 1,563 batted balls); a gap of 24.5 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 17.5 percentage points (rung 3 of 3, the 90th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,516 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a career ground-ball starter takes the air out of an offence that lives on balls in the air, so the lineup facing the higher ground-ball share is the disadvantaged side and club-level pricing averages the collision out. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 606be696ff199952.)

mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_lineup_vs_opposing_starter

thesis: Backing the away side of h2h_1st_5_innings because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) lineup_vs_primary_pitch -- this lineup's measured production against the primary pitch of the starter it faces (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 0.351 wOBA, home 0.304 wOBA (this game's own values rest on: away over 2,782 plate appearances; home over 696 plate appearances); a gap of 0.047 wOBA, clearing the threshold of 0.029 wOBA (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,048 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter who leans on one pitch, against a lineup that has measurably hit that pitch, has nowhere to hide for eighteen outs; the market prices his season line, not tonight's specific collision. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome e8c58d079df7ecdd.)

thesis: Backing the away side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) starter_groundball_share -- the opposing starter's career ground-ball share (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 36.9%, home 61.4% (this game's own values rest on: away over 176 batted balls; home over 1,563 batted balls); a gap of 24.5 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 17.5 percentage points (rung 3 of 3, the 90th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,516 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a career ground-ball starter takes the air out of an offence that lives on balls in the air, so the lineup facing the higher ground-ball share is the disadvantaged side and club-level pricing averages the collision out. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md).
